Football.title: £63m Chelsea star opens door to Barcelona move amid Cole Palmer and Enzo Fernandez uncertainty
Football.content:
When it rains, it pours.

Amid reports Cole Palmer and Enzo Fernandez could seek a move away from Stamford Bridge, a third Chelsea star has now cast doubt over his future at the club.

3 Palmer could lead a mass exodus from Stamford Bridge in the summer Credit: Getty

Speaking while on international duty with Spain, Blues defender Marc Cucurella was quizzed on whether he'd entertain a move to Barcelona.

On your Marc

"Let's see, it's clear that if those situations arise, well, they are hard to turn down, but I would consider it in the end," Cucurella said.

"It is not just me. I also have to think perhaps about my family, and together we would decide what is best for us.

"But, as I have said before, right now I am not thinking about that.

"It it comes, it will come, and we will see what decision is made."

It would mark an emotional return for Cucurella, who first joined the Spanish giants in 2012 and spent eight years on their books before moving to Getafe in June 2020.

However, Cucurella was only a permanent player at Getafe for just one season as Brighton came calling in August 2021.

Cucurella's impressive displays for the Seagulls caught the eyes of the Premier League's heavyweight clubs, as Chelsea beat Manchester City in the race for his signature having agreed a £63million deal.

The Spaniard has a contract until 2028.

Cucurella's comments are the latest in what has been a worrying few days for Blues supporters when it comes to the futures of key players.

3 Cucurella has made over 150 appearances for the Blues Credit: Getty

Palmed off?

Reports emerged over the weekend Palmer could be tempted to push for an exit amid frustrations with Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior's tactics.

Real Madrid, Manchester United and Bayern Munich have all been credited with an interest in Palmer, although a mooted £150m price tag could put the trio off.

Further muddying the waters is the fact all three clubs already have players who boast a similar profile to Palmer, with Gabby Agbonlahor unconvinced Real Madrid even want the England international.

What Fer?

Palmer hasn't been as explicit about his uncertain future as teammate Fernandez, who has continually dropped hints he could leave the Blues.

Fernandez ignited rumours about his future following the second leg of Chelsea's defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last 16 when he could not confirm he'd be at Stamford Bridge after the World Cup.

The Argentina international fanned the flames when he seemingly took a swipe at Chelsea's board regarding their decision to part ways with Enzo Maresca in January.

3 Rosenior may be in for a summer of transfer drama Credit: Getty

Fernandez has now claimed he could see himself living in Spain, stating: "I really like Madrid - it's similar to Buenos Aires."

The World Cup winner's comments will only fuel rumours he wants a move to Real Madrid.

talkSPORT understands Fernandez is open to a move to the Spanish giants in the summer, but Real are yet to take any formal steps towards making the switch a reality.

Whatever happens, it promises to be a noisy few months for Blues boss Rosenior.

Football.title: Roberto De Zerbi move ‘screams desperation’ as Tottenham fans told to get ready for the Championship
Football.content:
Roberto De Zerbi move ‘screams desperation’ as Tottenham fans told to get ready for the Championship

Roberto De Zerbi's imminent arrival as Tottenham Hotspur manager has already split opinions amongst supporters.

The Italian is set to be confirmed as Igor Tudor's successor on a five-year deal with the immediate mission to stop Spurs from suffering a first relegation in 49 years.

5 De Zerbi's imminent arrival as Spurs manager is set to split opinion amongst fans Credit: Getty

However, De Zerbi's arrival could prove to be divisive amongst the fan base of the north London club.



The Women of the Lane fan group have already urged the club not to appoint De Zerbi due to his comments on Mason Greenwood whilst Marseille manager.

De Zerbi previously spent just under two years as Brighton manager, during which time he achieved their highest-ever league finish.

His subsequent spell at Marseille ended in February after he was sacked by the French giants.

Ahead of De Zerbi's unveiling, talkSPORT hosts and pundits have given their verdicts on his appointment.



Paul Hawksbee

Speaking on Monday's Hawksbee and Jacobs, Paul Hawksbee explained: "Look, he did a great job at Brighton. I remember speaking to some of the people down at Brighton when he first took over and they were very excited.

"Two caveats. One being that he’s already been a divisive figure.

"Some of the fan groups at Spurs weren’t happy about comments he made about Mason Greenwood while at Marseille. They’ve had a ‘No to De Zerbi’ campaign."



He continued: "Day one, I think you’ll have to qualify some of the things he said because we don’t need any more division among the fan base. We’ve had enough of that already.

"The other thing is, one of his problems at Brighton was he wanted more involvement in transfers.



5

"I think he is quite impatient and he expects good players to be bought for him to allow him to do his job. Tottenham’s track record is going to change drastically on that front.

"In all the years of ENIC, it has not been good. This is how they’ve got themselves into this mess, by not paying the wages and not signing the talent."

'Screams desperation'

Fellow Spurs fan Majestic has also revealed his stance on the decision to replace Tudor with De Zerbi.

Speaking to talkSPORT.com, the Inside Spurs host explained: "Tottenham Hotspur signing Roberto De Zerbi as the new manager I've got to be honest with you, screams desperation.



"I agree De Zerbi is a competent manager and a good tactician, but let's be real here. Thomas Frank, everyone thought we were too good for him. What's he ever done? He's only been at Brentford.

"Yes, De Zerbi got Brighton to sixth in his first season in the Premier League, but after that he finished 11th. What else has he done?

5 Appointing the 'volatile' De Zerbi 'screams desperation' according to Majestic Credit: Getty

"And for me, Spurs have played all of their cards on the table that they're in a position now where De Zerbi, who already rejected them, is able to hold all of the aces and ask for a five-year deal.

"For me, the real problem with De Zerbi is his temperament. The man's got a reputation for being volatile, clashing with the press and falling out with other managers, losing it on the touchline.



"And when you're fighting for your life in a relegation battle, what do you need? You need a calm, cool, steady hand. You need someone to stabilise the ship, not someone who's gonna blow a gasket at the first setback.

"And here's what really annoys me about this board. We had the likes of Tim Sherwood, Harry Redknapp, even ex-England international manager Glenn Hoddle. That's right, club legend Glenn Hoddle all put their hand up to say, ‘I'll help out and keep this club up for free’. And what does the board do? Completely ignore him.

"And they hand De Zerbi one of the best paid positions in English football on a five-year deal.

"That's not football thinking, that's not for the fans, that's not for the good of the club, that's for their own pure vanity. That's the board saying we know best, even though they got it completely wrong with Igor Tudor and Thomas Frank.

5 Spurs fans have not seen their side win a Premier League match since December Credit: Getty



"Spurs, well, the board, have been bullied into this by their own blind pride. And you know what? That might be the move right there that sends Tottenham Hotspur down to the Championship. And the scary part is, I don't know when you get back."

Too little too late?

Meanwhile, Sonny Snelling, another member of the Inside Spurs team told talkSPORT.com: "I have mixed feelings about it. This is probably the appointment that should’ve been made before Igor Tudor because you would’ve had more games for De Zerbi to get his style of play across.

"What we saw from his Brighton and Marseille teams were quite revolutionary. Pep Guardiola said he was one of the most influential coaches over the last 20 years. The way he used to do those box formations, the 4-2-2-2 was amazing.

"But Tottenham don’t have the players to play this formation at present. If he came in over the summer and overhauled the squad you’d back it even more.

"Think of Guglielmo Vicario and Antonin Kinsky, are they confident enough with the ball to play it out the back? Our midfield, even Conor Gallagher and Joao Palhinha, Rodrigo Bentancur, Archie Gray, Pape Matar Sarr, are any of them confident enough on the ball to dictate the play? I’m not so sure on that.



"When it’s fully ticking there’s no doubt De Zerbi is one of the best coaches in world football.

5 Snelling doubts whether Spurs' players are 'confident' enough for De Zerbi's tactical approach Credit: Getty

"My other issue is can he get on with the board? He falls out with most boards he works with, he doesn’t last long at football clubs.

"A lot to be concerned about but the proof will be in the pudding."

De Zerbi is a 'top manager' - O'Hara

However, Jamie O'Hara is adamant De Zerbi is a good appointment for his old club.

The former Spurs midfielder admits he has been surprised by the reaction of fans opposed to his arrival.



Speaking on The Sports Bar, O'Hara revealed: "I'm a bit annoyed and a bit upset. Some Spurs fans who I've seen all over social media, they don't want De Zerbi. They're not having him.

"In what planet do we think that we can dictate what manager we get. Roberto De Zerbi is a top Premier League manager. Top manager.

"He led Brighton to a sixth place finish, the highest ever in their history. He plays fantastic football and his win percentage in the Premier League, 42.7% with Brighton.

"He is a top manager, he's in the game, he knows the Premier League. He's fresh.

"We're not talking about getting like a Harry Redknapp or a Tim Sherwood. They did good jobs, but we're talking about a manager who's at the top of his game. And people are moaning about him coming in.



"I don't get the argument, I don't get it. We're in dire straits right now. And we're getting a top quality manager who's going to come in and hopefully galvanise this group of players for seven games.

"And then beyond that, then he can really work on becoming the manager that we all think he was going to be when he left Brighton. Everyone was obviously saying how good he was then. He went to Marseille and did well at Marseille.

"I just don't get this narrative around him that we think we're too good for Roberto De Zerbi. It's crazy."

Football.title: Two Euro 2028 tickets to cost less than parking at 2026 World Cup
Football.content:
Two Euro 2028 tickets to cost less than parking at 2026 World Cup

The cheapest tickets for Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland are set to cost under £30 - a stark contrast to prices at the upcoming World Cup.

UEFA committed to ensuring that 40 per cent of tickets are in the 'most affordable categories'.

3 Infantino presented the first ever FIFA 'peace prize' to Donald Trump Credit: GETTY

At EURO 2024 in Germany, UEFA set prices in the cheapest group at £26 and £52, with plans to keep prices similar at the following tournament.



And it's reported at the next Euros, which takes places in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, that 15 per cent of tickets will be available for £30 or less and a further 25 per cent will cost below £60.

This measure is at odds for what English football fans experience when watching their clubs with ticket prices on the rise.

For Premier League teams, the main source of revenue comes from broadcasting deals and commercial sponsorship.

Yet clubs have focused on increasing matchday revenue with fans paying a hefty price as these teams target tourists who are willing to pay a premium.



Liverpool recently caused outrage. While major expansions at Anfield increased the ground's capacity to 61,000, but the number of season ticket holders remains the same.

This allows the Premier League champions to sell nearly 50 per cent of tickets on a match-by-match basis, enabling the Reds to target neutral fans and tourists who are willing to spend more on the matchday experience.



Additionally, hospitality is not designed for the average fan with the most expensive option at the Etihad for Manchester City's upcoming fixture with Arsenal on April 19 available for £5,500.

By comparison, the prices for the World Cup were first released last December on general sale with prices ranging from $140 (£106) which emerged as the cheapest to $8,680 (£6,564) for the final.



Additionally, a ticket stateside is just the beginning - parking in Texas at the AT&T Stadium would cost $75 (£57) - the same price as two Euro 2028 tickets.

3 England reached the final of Euro 2024 but lost to Spain Credit: Getty

FIFA began a minor price decrease after a major uproar from fans, allowing just ten per cent of fans in a qualified nation to get the cheapest tickets which are fixed at $60 (£45).

The tournament's ticket prices were initially seven times more expensive than the World Cup in Qatar until a cheaper option was created.

There are also no concessions for children, seniors or other groups.

A summer of 'soccer'

This summer will be the first time a tournament has three host countries (USA, Mexico and Canada) and will be an opportunity for America to show its growing love of football.



When the country hosted its first tournament in 1994, a poll found that 71 per cent of America didn't know it was happening and the other 29 per cent didn't care.

This time, the demand for tickets is vastly different, with FIFA receiving 500 million ticket applications in the last lottery.

3 Many fans are travelling to America, even without tickets Credit: AFP

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has a close relationship with Donald Trump which led to the US president receiving the inaugural 'peace prize'.

FIFA's final ticket window for the World Cup opens on April 1, with additional tickets being made available for general purchase.



There will be a record-breaking 104 matches due to an increase to 48 teams involved and every match is expected to be sold out.

Despite the demand still clearly being there for the World Cup, UEFA still took a subtle dig stating they're committed to a 'fair, transparent and fan-first ticketing process.'

Football.title: Elliot Anderson responds to Man United and Man City transfer speculation
Football.content:
Elliot Anderson insists he is fully focused on making England's World Cup squad, despite continued speculation over his future.

The Nottingham Forest midfielder has been widely tipped for a big-money move in the summer, with both Manchester City and Manchester United keen on securing his services.

5 Anderson discussed what the coming months will look like for him but didn't give a lot awau Credit: Getty

After making a name for himself at the City Ground, City are understood to be prepared to step up their interest in Anderson.



Regarded as a potential successor for Rodri, the Citizens believe the 23-year-old favours a move to them over neighbours United.

Anderson wouldn't come cheap though, having been valued in the region of £100million, and this figure could rise even more if he impresses on the world stage this summer.

Despite only making his England debut in September, the Forest star looks nailed on for Thomas Tuchel's squad to go to the World Cup.

He is expected to line up alongside Arsenal star Declan Rice at the base of Tuchel's favoured 4-2-3-1 setup.



Tunnel vision

While rumours continue to swirl about where Anderson could be playing next season, he insisted his only focus is performing for club and country in the coming months.

Before the prospect of a World Cup, he is looking to help Forest maintain their Premier League status, who are locked in a relegation battle.



Speaking ahead of England's friendly clash with Japan on Tuesday, live on talkSPORT, Anderson insisted he has given little thought to much else.

He said: "Obviously we’ve got the World Cup this summer so all my eyes are on that.



"Playing for England, I’ve got the badge on now so that’s all I’m thinking about at the moment.

5 Anderson is expected to line up alongside Declan Rice for England at the World Cup this summer Credit: Getty

5 The Forest star has seven games left of the Premier League season to help his club avoid relegation Credit: Getty

Asked if he felt confident he would be in the team at the start of the tournament, Anderson replied: “I want it that way. But I’ve got a season left with Forest.

"I’ve got plenty of games and there’s plenty of time until then. I’ve got to keep my standards high and make sure that happens."



England star Elliot

Anderson is in line to start against Japan, which will be his last chance to impress before Tuchel names his final World Cup squad in May.

He was among 11 players to join up late with England group after their first friendly against Uruguay - an encouraging sign in itself.

All 11 stars appeared certainties to be included in the Three Lions' World Cup squad at the very least, or in Tuchel's first XI.

After forging a strong pairing with Rice in his first six international appearances, Anderson will have a different midfield partner against Japan,with the Arsenal star being forced to withdraw through injury.

5 The Forest star has impressed Tuchel in his six England caps so far Credit: Getty



5 Rice looks set for a fourth major tournament at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

And the Forest man credited Rice for helping him to make the step-up on the international stage.

On Rice, Anderson said: "It’s a really good partnership. Since I’ve come in, he’s made me feel comfortable, he’s helped me learn on the job.

"He’s full of energy to help me and the relationship on the pitch is really good. [He’s helped me] on and off the pitch.

“Seeing the way he plays on the pitch, I’m trying to learn from him. Little things on the training pitch, bits of advice, putting his arm around me and just building on the relationship."

News.title: Three people including girl, 18, charged with murder of ‘beautiful’ teen, 16, who was found ‘stabbed in back’ in street
News.content:
TEEN HORROR Three people including girl, 18, charged with murder of ‘beautiful’ teen, 16, who was found ‘stabbed in back’ in street

THREE people including an 18-year-old girl have been charged with the murder of a teen found stabbed in the back in the street.

Chloe Watson, 16, was attacked after a party in Austhorpe, Leeds, at 5.55am on Saturday.





Officers discovered the teenager, from the Cleckheaton area, with serious injuries in the middle of the street.

She was rushed to hospital where medical professionals sadly pronounced her dead a short time later.

Three people have now been charged with murder and are due to appear at Leeds Magistrates’ Court today.

They are Kayla Smith, 18, Archie Rycroft, 19, and a 17-year-old boy who cannot legally be named.



West Yorkshire Police said all three define their ethnicities as White British.

An 18-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder remains in custody.

A further 18-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl who were arrested on suspicion of murder have been released on bail pending further enquiries.

The charges come after Chloe’s distraught mum paid tribute to her “beautiful princess”, saying: “I cannot put into words how I feel that you are not here with me.



“You are my life, my world, my best friend and I know that I am yours. I cannot live without you – I need you.

“You are stunning, confident, loyal, honest and my family-oriented princess.

“When you walk into any room it lights up with your bubbly personality. There is so much I could say. There’s a big hole in my heart that can never be filled.

“Your two sisters and big brother will always love and miss you to infinity. You will always and forever be in our hearts. Love Mum, Connor, Courtney and Cienna.”

Her father’s family also issued a tribute in the wake of the killing describing their “immeasurable” heartache.



It read: “We miss every single thing about her. She was beautiful, full of joy, and had a wonderfully cheeky personality.

“She embraced life with such happiness, and she had her whole future ahead of her.

“Chloe was loved by everyone who knew her, and the absence she leaves behind is immeasurable.

“We will miss her forever, she will never be forgotten.”

A GoFundMe has since been set up by Chloe’s cousin Shantelle.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A local claimed Chloe was “stabbed in the back” on Saturday morning as other residents rallied around to try and save her.

The force is still looking to hear from people who could help with their investigation.

News.title: National inquiry into grooming gangs scandal finally begins today – but could last until 2029
News.content:
THE national inquiry into the grooming gangs scandal will finally begin today and could last until 2029.

After months of delays, ministers have promised it will focus on whether ethnicity and religion played a role.





In many cases, victims were young white girls preyed on by gangs of Asian men, mostly of Pakistani origin.

Sir Keir Starmer spent months resisting an inquiry and only approved one following pressure from tech billionaire Elon Musk and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch.

The £65million inquiry has powers to force witnesses to give evidence and demand documents. Investigators will examine how grooming gangs operated and how police, councils, health services and schools responded.

They will also assess why victims were often ignored or blamed for their suffering.



Crucially, lawyers will probe how the ethnicity, culture or religion of perpetrators and survivors influenced patterns of offending — and the response of public services.

Oldham is among the first areas to face a probe. More locations will be named within three months.

Former Children’s Commissioner, Baroness Anne Longfield will chair the probe.

It will run no later than March 2029. She said: “We will follow the evidence wherever it leads. We will not flinch from uncomfortable truths.”



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: “We have agreed that the inquiry will explicitly examine the role of ethnicity, religion and culture of the offenders and in the response of institutions.”

News.title: Scots gangland kingpin Steven Lyons pictured in orange jumpsuit as he’s escorted by cops at Bali police HQ after arrest
News.content:
GANGLAND boss Steven Lyons has been pictured in an orange prisoner jumpsuit being escorted by cops following his arrest.

The wanted hood was nicked in Bali, Indonesia, on Saturday after being on the run.





The 45-year-old, a member of the notorious Glasgow Lyons gang, was arrested amid a major multi-agency police operation, which also led to arrests in Scotland and Spain.

Over the weekend, Lyons was paraded by Indonesian officers after he was apprehended at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport on a flight from Singapore.

He has now been pictured dressed in an orange high-vis jumpsuit and black face mask with his hands in cable ties at police headquarters in Denpasar as he faces doing time in Bali’s hellhole Keobokan jail.

An underworld source said: “It’s an incredible demise for Steven Lyons whose world has fallen apart in the space of a year.

Read more Scottish news GANG BOSS NICKED Moment notorious Brit crime boss is paraded by Bali cops after arrest

“His brother and best pal murdered, his wife nicked in Dubai and members of his gang lifted in Spain and Scotland.

“This is a stunning development that will delight his enemies but you have to wonder why he didn’t live a quiet life with all the money he has made.

“It’s the end of the Lyons gang’s dominance in Glasgow.

“Getting involved in this gang war was the biggest mistake of his life – it has backfired spectacularly.”



We first told of Lyons’ growing paranoia in January last year when he used a lie detector in a bid to root out rats in his camp in the wake of several police raids on drug stashes across Glasgow.

Just two months later, the first firebomb attack linked to the turf war sparked a year of bloodshed and violence with associates of caged hood Mark Richardson and the Daniel clan in the firing line.

Then in May Eddie Lyons Jnr and Ross Monaghan were gunned down in a Spanish bloodbath – with Steven unable to return to Scotland for their funerals.

He was later booted out of Dubai in September only to end up in Bali where he was nicked the day after his crew was targeted in an international sting.

Then wife Amanda was snared in Dubai as the Lyons criminal empire crumbled with rivals convinced they will never recover.



The crime network headed up by Steven was the subject of a dramatic cross border operation that saw 13 suspects nicked in dawn raids across Scotland and Spain on Friday.

News.title: Teen sent desperate message to pal asking to be picked up from party before being ‘stabbed in back in row over boy’
News.content:
A TEENAGE girl found stabbed to death after leaving an “out of hand” house party sent a desperate message to a pal begging to be picked up moments before being attacked.

Chloe Watson Dransfield, 16, was found fatally injured on the road in Leeds shortly before 6am on Saturday – after allegedly being stabbed in the back.





She was rushed to hospital where she tragically died from her injuries.

Five people – including two woman aged 18, a man aged 19 and two boys aged 17 – remain in police custody on suspicion of murder.

A friend told of how Chloe had wanted to leave the address, describing the gathering as “getting out of hand”.



They said: “Chloe wanted to go. It was all getting out of hand and people were inhaling balloons of laughing gas.

“She contacted a friend telling them to pick her up. But it was too late.

“She tried to get out to get help, only to collapse on the road.

“Neighbours came rushing out and tried to give her CPR while the emergency services were on their way.



“She was only 16 and had her whole life ahead of her. It’s just devastating.”

This comes as a local claimed Chloe was “stabbed in the back” and other residents rallied around to try and save her.

Wayne Mallows, 64, told the Daily Mail: “She had been stabbed in the back and there was quite a bit of blood. Her eyes were just blank.

“I was called out about 5.50am by a dog walker. She said my neighbour was doing CPR on a young girl but he was getting tired.

“I asked if they’d rung an ambulance, and I realised that a phone was on the ground and he had it on loudspeaker. Ambulance control were giving him instructions.”



Wayne said he then took over before the ambulance arrived a few minutes later.

Chloe’s family released a heart breaking statement paying tribute to the tragic teenager.

Her distraught mum wrote: “I cannot put into words how I feel that you are not here with me.

“You are my life, my world, my best friend and I know that I am yours. I cannot live without you – I need you.

“You are stunning, confident, loyal, honest and my family-oriented princess.



“When you walk into any room it lights up with your bubbly personality. There is so much I could say. There’s a big hole in my heart that can never be filled.

“Your two sisters and big brother will always love and miss you to infinity. You will always and forever be in our hearts. Love Mum, Connor, Courtney and Cienna.”

Her father’s family also issued a tribute in the wake of the senseless killing describing their “immeasurable” heartache.

It read: “We miss every single thing about her. She was beautiful, full of joy, and had a wonderfully cheeky personality.

“She embraced life with such happiness, and she had her whole future ahead of her.



“Chloe was loved by everyone who knew her, and the absence she leaves behind is immeasurable.

“We will miss her forever, she will never be forgotten.”

An online fundraising page set up by a relative suggested Chloe’s life had been taken away “in a flash over a boy”.



The post, by Chloe’s cousin Shantelle, said: “I’m setting up a Gofundme for my 16 year old cousin whose life was sadly taken in tragedy.

“16 years young didn’t even make it to her 18th. Her whole life was taken in a flash over a boy.

“Her mum is distraught she has left two younger siblings behind she was sadly murdered.

“I wanted to create a Gofundme to help give her the best send off possible. She didn’t deserve this, she was so full of life. Such an innocent, beautiful soul taken too soon.”

Residents desperately tried to save Chloe’s life before she was taken to hospital.



Tributes were left at the scene of the alleged murder in Kennerleigh Avenue, a suburb of east Leeds consisting mainly of bungalows populated by elderly residents.

One of the messages read: “Rest easy, my Chloe. Love you forever my crazy girl”. Another paid tribute to “my beautiful girl”.

Looking at the tributes, local resident Gillian Brook said: “This area’s really quiet. This young girl’s lost her life. She’d got all her life ahead of her.

“My granddaughter’s the same age.

“My heart goes out to her family and everybody who knew her. It’s devastating.



“It’s just a really quiet area and you don’t expect it. It’s so, so sad.”

Another resident, who asked not to be named, said: “It’s a very quiet road – lots of bungalows and retired people.

“It’s absolutely heartbreaking that a girl so young has lost her life.

“Everyone is in disbelief. You hear about these things happening elsewhere, but you never expect it on your own street. It’s terribly sad.”

Detective Chief Superintendent Marc Bowes, of West Yorkshire Police, has appealed for anyone who was in the area and witnessed what happened to come forward with information.



He said: “This is an extremely complex investigation where a young woman has sadly lost her life.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you can assist this investigation then please call the Homicide and Major Enquiry Team on 101, or use the live chat options at http://www.westyorkshire.police.uk/livechat, quoting log 280 of 28 March.

You can also report anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or online.

News.title: Ex-nude glamour model who dined with King Charles slams critics after being appointed honorary consul to holiday hotspot
News.content:
A FORMER model who once dined with King Charles has been appointed as Ukraine’s honorary consul to the Dominican Republic.

Victoria Yakimova’s appointment by Volodymyr Zelensky‘s foreign ministry has reportedly “raised eyebrows” in Kyiv.





However, the former glamour model insists she is not ashamed of her raunchy past.

“I did not try to conceal my previous life associated with modelling,” she said.

“The modern self-sufficient woman has the right to realise herself in her chosen profession, as well as to change the direction of development and growth.”

However, many people have taken issue with this.

Influencer Marina Danilchuk said: “I don’t know what’s better in this story: the naked breasts of the consul on social media or her photo in kokoshniks [Russian headdresses].

“I went to this lady’s social networks and everywhere in one line it says that she is consul and she is a model.

“It’s strange to combine such areas, but, you know, Ukraine is very rich in talents.



“Among these photos in panties, on my word of honour, in swimsuits, I managed to find official photos that confirm that this lady is indeed now the consul of Ukraine in the Dominican Republic.”

Others have jumped to her defence, including former MP Boryslav Bereza.

However, the parliamentarian did admit “many did not like the new honorary consul of Ukraine in the Dominican [Republic].”

The 37-year-old beauty claims she has received no handouts from the state.

“There is no government funding for this position, so my operations and all associated expenses are my personal contribution and my family’s contribution,” she said.



Yakimova also revealed she has been living in the Dominican Republic since 2014 and had been married to one of its citizens.

The Odesa-born widow later insisted on her loyalty to Ukraine.

“I urge everyone to support the Armed Forces of Ukraine and our volunteers. Glory to Ukraine,” she said.

In 2017, Yakimova met the future King Charles.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking about her encounter with the then Prince of Wales, she said: “It was an interesting experience; the atmosphere at the palace is incredible, and of course it’s something you remember – something I could never have imagined would happen to me.



“I have so much respect [for him].”

News.title: Brit snowboarder, 43, dies after falling 320ft from off-piste rocky ledge at top ski resort amid spate of slope deaths
News.content:
MOUNTAIN TRAGEDY Brit snowboarder, 43, dies after falling 320ft from off-piste rocky ledge at top ski resort amid spate of slope deaths

A BRIT snowboarder has tragically died after plunging over 300 feet off a rocky ledge at a French ski resort.

The 43-year-old, who has not been named, is thought to have been snowboarding alone off-piste on the slopes of La Plagne.





A spokesman for the Modane police mountain rescue unit said: “The victim is thought to have fallen at least one hundred meters (320 feet) on Saturday from a rocky ledge in an off-piste area.

“The emergency services were alerted to the disappearance at around 2.15pm and patrols were sent out.

“Rescuers soon determined that the missing British man had last been seen using the ski lifts in the Bécoin area of La Plagne.”

Emergency services rushed to the scene, but the Brit was declared dead at the scene and his body was airlifted away by helicopter.



A probe has been launched by a local prosecutor to explain the tragedy.

La Plagne, which Brit holidaymakers flock to in their droves every winter, is one of the most popular ski resorts in the world and attracts more than 2.5million visitors a season.

Excluding avalanches, 31 people have died in the French ski resorts this year, with 18 coming from the collisions, according to France‘s National Mountain Safety organisation.

Since the start of the season, more than 30 people have been killed by avalanches in France, including six on the weekend of January 10 to 11.



Huge avalanches have swept Europe this winter leaving record fatalities in their wake.

The death toll across France, Italy, Switzerland and Austria has already climbed above 60 this season alone.

The disasters are caused by an “unusually weak” snowpack, the total snow from the ground to the snow surface, according to experts.

Fresh snow builds above this “weak base”, making all additional layers “very unstable”.

Avalanche expert Alain Duclos told The Sun that Europe must brace for more avalanches – which will be “wider and more powerful”.



He said: “I’m afraid that more fatalities will happen.”

The Brit snowboarder’s death comes as a 41-year-old tourist was buried by an enormous 820ft-wide avalanche buried him in Austria.

Federico Giubilato was skiing off piste with a friend when tragedy struck.

The extreme sports enthusiast, who would have turned 42 years old on Monday, was crushed by about 5.2ft of ice.



His pal was able to break free from the snow with just a hand injury.

The 36-year-old was then able to call for help.

Mountain rescue services scrambled to the scene in two helicopters, arriving around half an hour later.

Emergency crews desperately tried to save Federico by digging through the ice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It took 30 minutes to reach his body, by which time the mechanical engineer had tragically died.



The pair, from Bassano del Grappa, in northern Italy, were skiing in Marchkopf, Austria, when the avalanche hit on Saturday afternoon.

News.title: Agony for Ted Lasso star Hannah Waddingham as her grandad and Britain’s oldest war veteran dies aged 109
News.content:
BRITAIN’S oldest war veteran – actress Hannah Waddingham’s grandad – has died, age 109.

Royal Navy gunner Harry Waddingham became Britain’s oldest surviving veteran last July on the death of 110-year-old Donald Rose.





Announcing his death, the East Sussex Branch of the Royal Navy Association said Harry was ‘Truly one of the last of our greatest generation.’

And added: “He lived a long and full life and he will be greatly missed. RIP Shipmate, your duty is done, we have the watch.”

At last year’s Royal British Legion Festival of Remembrance, his proud granddaughter Ted Lasso star Hannah paid a moving tribute to her war hero granddad who served on six ships and survived the sinking of two of them.



Born in 1916, he served from the first to the last day of World War II in the Royal Navy.

Harry served in the Royal Navy from 1932 rising from able seaman to sub lieutenant.

Of the six ships he served on, two were sunk during his time on them.

On the 29 May 1940 HMS Wakeful was picking up soldiers from the Dunkirk beach evacuation when she was hit by a torpedo from a German E-boat.



Wakeful was split in two with the forward part sinking immediately.

Recalling the experience, Harry said: “Really you never slept and my memory of those days was constant tiredness.

“And hardly being able to stand.



“But suddenly there was a bang and the ship went down.

“Those who were on the outer part of the upper deck must have been catapulted into the air and dropped into the sea.

“There were 600 soldiers plus a ship’s crew of about 200.



“Only those on the upper deck survived.”

Only one of the 640 soldiers survived with 25 of the ship’s company – Harry being one of them.

A year later he was on HMS Juno evacuating Crete when she came under high level bombing attack from enemy aircraft.



She was hit by three bombs which split the ship in two, sinking her in two minutes.

Harry recalled: “I didn’t like the Juno.

“I was only on there as a replacement for somebody, I was only on it about six months.

“We were in the evacuation of Crete and it’s hard to imagine it now but we were bringing back a ship load of soldiers.

“We were sunk by flights and flights of German and Italian aircraft. We were taking people from Crete to Alexandria in Egypt.



“On the way back we were sunk again by huge air attacks and the ship just turned over again. I was always a gunner on the upper deck.

“It wasn’t the most comfortable position but if the ship was going to sink it was a good place to be.”

He also served on north Atlantic convoys and Russian convoys.

He said: “An Atlantic convoy used to take about three-and-a-half weeks.

“Although those 3,000 miles you didn’t go straight across.



“We would go in long, 100-mile zig zags to avoid submarines.

“During that time at any moment you could be called to action stations so you never got undressed.

“You showered and put on clean clothes in Halifax, Nova Scotia and the next time you took them off was in Liverpool three-and-a-half weeks later.

“Almost every night we saw ships being blown up.

“The U boats were very clever and very brave.



“And oddly enough most sinkings were done with the U boat already on the surface.

“Once they fired their torpedo then they dived.

“But they were very accurate and they almost won the war.

“It was very close.”

He also served in the North Sea aboard HMS Mendip as a member of a gun crew.



“Action stations really was pandemonium,” he said.

“You were expected to be all positions ready in two to three minutes.

“Now if you’re going from the after mess deck to somewhere else it’s a long way to go.

“I wore a balaclava then I had a leather motorcycle helmet and then I had another balaclava with holes cut out for the eyes and I wore that back to front which kept me warm.

“The four corners around the gun turret which was constantly moving left or right according to where they were firing there were four spring loaded flat hatches.



“Your job was to grasp the oil-covered projectile and put it with brass cartridge attached out from the deck.

“When the gun fired it ejected the brass cartridge quite rapidly that if it hit you it would knock you over.

“So you had to keep out of the way of ejected brass cartridges and at the same time keep groping around below foot level to pull out another cartridge.

“Your hands were cold you couldn’t wear gloves because they’d be caught in the mechanism of the gun.

“I spent my 25th birthday in a destroyer’s mess deck when everybody offers you his rum.



“And my shipmate – my particular shipmate – said, ‘make the most of your 25th Harry because the way this going you may not see your 26th’.

“I remember that.”

At the end of the war, having obtained a degree in marine physics, he was discharged with the rank of lieutenant.

He added: “I was proud of the Navy.

“Without the Navy we would never have won the war.



“Hitler was ready to invade.

“But after Dunkirk we kept seven destroyer flotillas along the vulnerable coast.

“Had Hitler attempted to invade he may have had aerial supremacy but not at sea.”

He became a school teacher but then got a post with the RAF educational wing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He subsequently retired from the RAF with the rank of squadron leader.



He later taught at Archbishop Tenison’s School. Croydon where he ran the military cadets and moved to Bexhill-on-Sea, East Sussex where he died.

News.title: Man, 53, who died after ‘blowing up’ his house over £80 rent rise told friends ‘it’s going out with a bang’
News.content:
GAS VOW Man, 53, who died after ‘blowing up’ his house over £80 rent rise told friends ‘it’s going out with a bang’

A DAD was upset by a £90 rent increase and threatening to blow up his house on the day he died in an explosion, an inquest has heard.

David Howard was found in the rubble of his home in Worksop, Nottinghamshire, in April last year.





A post-mortem examination found the 53-year-old died from asphyxia caused by being trapped following the incident at around 7.40pm on April 12 2025.

The inquest was told he was communicating with emergency services for up to 90 minutes before he died, reports the BBC.

A toxicology report found Howard had low levels of heroin, cocaine and alcohol in his system.

He had been diagnosed with PTSD and struggled with his mental health for several years.

Detective Constable Daniel Akehurst, from Nottinghamshire Police, told the inquest had established Howard was angry after finding out his rent was to be increased by £80.

He added on the day of the explosion, Howard had told friends he was going to blow up the house.

Pal Shanelle Williams, who spoke with him around 3.30pm that afternoon, told cops he’d said: “I’ve done it, I’ve pulled the pipes off the gas. It’s going to go with a bang.”



Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service carried out an investigation into the blast, which destroyed Howard’s home and damaging nearby properties.

Watch manager Christopher Trendowicz told the inquest he believed an electrical spark from the fridge freezer was the “most probable cause” of the explosion.

Assistant coroner Nathanael Hartley added the level of intoxicants in Howard’s blood might have led to “mild, cognitive impairment”, impacting his rational thinking.

He recorded a narrative conclusion, and said: “It is possible he did not appreciate the dangerousness of the situation.

“With that in mind, I find [Howard] did not intend to end his own life.”



Speaking at the time of the explosion, resident Jonathan Hodson described hearing an “almighty explosion” – adding: “Fence panels were rattling and the windows were shaking.”

Karolina Ciolko, who lives nearby, said: “I quickly looked out the window and saw smoke.

“The car in front of me rocked and the alarm went off. We quickly ran out of the house to see what had happened.”

News.title: BREAKING: Armed police storm Wrexham hotel in huge operation using battering rams
News.content:
Armed officers swooped on a UK hotel as guests reported seeing more than 10 police cars.

A major operation took place at Rossett Hall Hotel in Wrexham where witnesses reported seeing more than police vehicles race to the scene on Monday evening.

These included armed officers and police carrying battering rams at the hotel.

And now the hotel along with North Wales Police have issued statements about the incident where a person has been detained.

He stated: "Officers were called to an incident at a hotel in Rossett earlier today where a male was detained. I would like to reassure the community that this was an isolated incident, it was brought to a safe conclusion, and to thank them for their patience."

And a statement from the hotel read: "Following an incident at Rossett Hall this afternoon involving a vulnerable individual, we would like to express our sincere thanks to North Wales Police for their swift and professional response.

"The situation has now been fully resolved, and the hotel is operating as normal."

And this morning a spokesperson added: "A spokesperson for Rossett Hall said: “We are grateful to the police for their swift response and the situation has been resolved. I can confirm that all our guests and staff are absolutely fine and it’s business as usual at the hotel.”

News.title: Major update on grooming gangs inquiry as chair vows 'We won't flinch'
News.content:
The national inquiry into grooming gangs will directly examine whether ethnicity, culture or religion influenced offending - and whether it shaped the institutional response.

The probe has published its terms of reference, which will be laid before Parliament when it returns from recess on April 13. It will then begin its full investigation into the group-based sexual exploitation of children in England and Wales.

The long-awaited inquiry will look into how grooming gangs operated and how institutions, including the police, local authorities, health services, social care services and schools, responded to abuse.

It will have the legal powers to compel witnesses to give evidence and require organisations to hand over documents.

Any evidence of criminal conduct by professionals will be referred to Operation Beaconport, the national policing operation launched last year to review hundreds of previously closed investigations.

The inquiry will conduct local investigations in areas where serious failures have been identified in response to child sexual exploitation by grooming gangs. Oldham has been confirmed among the first areas.

The inquiry is being chaired by Baroness Anne Longfield, a former children's commissioner for England.

Lady Longfield said: "Children across England and Wales were and are sexually abused and exploited. When they asked for help, they were too often disbelieved, dismissed or blamed. That is the reality this inquiry exists to address.

"Victims and survivors have every right to ask whether this inquiry will be any different from those that came before.

"My answer is this: where we can, we will publish our findings as we go, not in a single report years from now. There will be no opportunity for institutions to quietly manage what we find.

"We will follow the evidence wherever it leads. We will not flinch from uncomfortable truths."

Lady Longfield will be supported by panellists Zoe Billingham, a former Her Majesty's Inspector of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services, and Eleanor Kelly, a former chief executive of Southwark Council.

The inquiry will hold public hearings, which will be live-streamed, and transcripts will be published after each hearing.

Findings will be published progressively rather than being held until a final report. The inquiry has a maximum duration of three years, to conclude no later than March 2029, and has a budget of £65 million.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "The grooming gangs scandal is one of the darkest moments in our country's history - where the most vulnerable people were abused and exploited at the hands of evil child rapists.

"The independent national inquiry will now begin its crucial work to uncover how these crimes were allowed to happen and root out failure wherever it occurred.

"The chair and I have agreed that the inquiry will be laser focused on grooming gangs and will explicitly examine the role of ethnicity, religion and culture of the offenders and in the response of institutions.

"There will be no hiding place for the predatory monsters who committed these vile crimes."

The grooming gangs inquiry was set up in response to a recommendation from Baroness Louise Casey's National Audit on Group-based Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse.

The audit found systemic failures and institutional paralysis had enabled grooming gangs to operate for many years.

News.title: Major manufacturing company Autostructures UK goes bust with hundreds at risk
News.content:
A UK specialist manufacturing company with a "reputation for excellence" has gone bust, placing hundreds of jobs at risk.

Autostructures UK, which played a pivotal role in helping JCB make the world's fastest tractor, has entered administration. The company worked alongside engineers at JCB to design and manufacture specialised wheel components for its Fastrac model, which can reach a peak speed of 153.771mph.

As a JCB supplier for 30 years, Autostructures UK supplied over 22,000 chassis over the course of a decade. It entered administration on March 27, according to The Gazette.

Joint administrators Christopher Pole, Ryan Grant and Sam Birchall from Interpath were called in two days prior to parent company, Moveero Ltd - which manufactures construction vehicles, as well as wheels, rims and hubs for farming.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

The company's UK arm became insolvent on March 26, with around 250 jobs at Sankey Holdings, Moveero Ltd and Autostructures UK at risk. The business was sold to private equity firm, Aurelius, in 2020.

Moveero group continues to operate profitably, Interpath said, with the rest of the group's businesses in the US and Denmark not affected by the insolvency in Britain. It explained that business based in the UK had faced major operational challenges due to a weakened off‑highway market, downward pricing pressure and competition from rivals.

"As a result of these ongoing challenges, the directors of the businesses have taken steps to protect the interests of creditors by appointing administrators," Inerpath said in a statement.

"This will allow the UK businesses to continue trading while buyers for the businesses and their assets are pursued, with all staff retained during this period."

David Geraghty, CEO of moveero, said: "Against a difficult economic backdrop, we have worked tirelessly over the past 12 months to improve the financial performance of the UK business.

"We are incredibly grateful for the support of our brilliant team and also the support of our customers who have provided us with funding in recent days which has given us the additional time we need to continue to explore the options available."

News.title: Mum says she has best-behaved children in UK thanks to diet and strict rule
News.content:
Mum says she has best-behaved children in UK thanks to diet and strict rule

Pam Johal says any parents can use her rules to improve their children's behaviour

Mum says she has best-behaved children in UK thanks to diet and strict rule

A mum-of-two claims to have the UK's best behaved kids thanks to two 'hacks' - but says some parents think they are too extreme. Pam Johal, 48, says she has always been complimented on how well-behaved her children, Henry, eight, and Georgie, nine, are in public.

‌



Even at home, she says the pair hardly ever step a toe out of line and for the past five years, the mum has avoided tantrums and dramatic meltdowns. According to Pam, the solution isn't rocket science but attributed to two easy habits parents can be doing right now.

‌



These include limiting screen time to almost zero and adopting a fruit-heavy diet - meaning they only eat uncooked fruits and vegetables. The changes came after the mum suffered from rheumatoid arthritis from the beginning of 2020, and by August, she claims she reversed the condition by eating fruit and cutting out lots of her favourite foods, including cheesy pasta and bacon sandwiches, for mangoes and avocado instead.

‌



View 5 Images Pam Johal, 48, mum to children Henry (8) and Georgie (9)

She also believes social media stunts development and brainwashes people into a false reality wanting her kids to grow up normal. Her children have adopted the same diet because Pam reckons a fruit smoothie a day keeps the doctor and sadness away as well as just 30 minutes of TV a day - for the past five years and says it was the best decision as her kids never get sick and hardly ever misbehave.

But despite the success of these habits, the mum admitted she doesn't gel with other parents who brand her techniques as extreme and out of touch. Pam, a health coach, from Southampton, Hampshire, said: "You shouldn't be raising your kids in front of a screen. Although, I agree they can be useful at certain times, you are damaging their growth. I give my children 30 minutes of screen time per day - and that's just for the TV.

‌



"Most of the time we are either out on walks, exercising or enjoying fruit. We never watch reality TV or drama addicting cr*p. It will always be a documentary or something educational. Those who solely rely on iPads or phones really need to change their ways.

View 5 Images Pam Johal, with her children Georgie and Henry

"Give them an apple or a toy. How do you think people like us from the 80s or 90s coped? Pam made the decision to raise her children plant-based almost five years ago after she claimed fruits "healed" her rheumatoid arthritis. She was diagnosed in 2020 after months of fatigue and muscle stiffness - and after a three-day retreat fasting along with fruit, she 'reversed' her condition.

‌



The National Center for Biotechnology Information says a raw vegan diet may decrease symptoms. Pam now lives on 90% fruit and has since been shocked at how much her life has improved and knew she wanted the same for her brood.

"My children are so much happier on fruit," Pam said. "Before, they'd been easily frustrated and agitated because their body wasn't getting what it needed. Now, I give them fruit smoothies in the morning - and put in anything I can like bananas, dates, pine nuts and mangos.

View 5 Images Pam Johal, 48, is a mum to children Henry (8) and Georgie (9)

‌



"It gives them all their daily vitamins on one drink and we haven't needed the GP since like other children. Sometimes, we give them a little treat - like a sweet. But that's on rare occasions because junk food isn't needed - they are always happy and I never have any troubles."

Pam claims her kids’ plant-based diet has stopped them from needing the doctor for childhood illnesses like the flu. But on top of their healthy eating, the mum also credits limiting their screen time to how well-behaved her kids are. She claims her and her husband, Simon, 47, an NHS admin, never have to deal with meltdowns or tantrums.

"It's OK for your kids to be bored," she said. "It allows them to grow and for them to come into themselves more - what they like and hate. Shoving a screen into their face for everything isn't right. It's damaging. I can happily and confidently go out to eat with my kids knowing they aren't going to kick up a fuss.

‌



View 5 Images The children eat a lot of fruit

"There's been many times where I've seen children having absolute meltdowns because they aren't online or playing Roblox. It's almost like a drug and they are getting withdrawals - and it's sad knowing many parents put up with it!" Pam said her children can have a phone once they have passed all their GCSEs and are 17 years of age.

She only lets them go to houses or out with people she 100% trusts. "I'm not worried they will fall behind," she said. It's about trust and knowing your kids will make the right decisions. I can't change the rest of the world, but I'm working with them so they can understand these things and be safe.

‌



"It's also to stop them from being lazy. Can you imagine what all this technology might be doing to their spine and mobility?"

The family do at least three hours a week of exercises, meditations and nature walks instead of relying on technology and Pam said she has cracked the code for parenting.

View 5 Images The family has a healthy diet

Article continues below

Since the change, she has noticed her kids listen, talk and are a lot more helpful around the house. "It's just built into them now," Pam said. "They are the best and always go out of their way to help others because they have time to work on their mindset.The technology isn't destroying their brain."

But despite her success, Pam says some parents have viewed her techniques as extreme and out of touch. "I think my habits make me quite unlikable with other parents - especially at school or in the playground," she said. "They don't think I'm serious or believe my ways are fake and don't work. But that couldn't be further from the case.

"I have cracked the code at parenting and if you spend one day with my family you can see what I'm talking about. We are happy, healthy and trouble-free. Which is more than what most parents can say."

News.title: Hit-and-run driver carried on delivering Chinese takeaway after leaving dad to die
News.content:
Hit-and-run driver carried on delivering Chinese takeaway after leaving dad to die

A takeaway driver was dubbed 'cruelly inhumane' after he crashed his car into a dad-of-two but didn't call and ambulance, instead fleeing from the scene

View 3 Images Daniel Wyke was sentenced after he slammed his car into a dogwalker (Image: WalesOnline)

A delivery driver carried on delivering Chinese takeaway after he slammed into a dog walker and left him to die before complaining about the damage to his vehicle.

‌



Dad-of-two Aaron Jones had been out walking his family's Labrador in his home village of Llanpumsaint, north of Carmarthen, Wales. A court has heard the frantic moments after takeaway driver Daniel Wyke, 28, smashed into the dad on a country lane while working.

‌



Aaron hit the car windshield and landed on the other side of a stone wall in a neighbouring churchyard on December 23, 2024. His heartbroken family, who described the dad as "a gentle and loving soul" said he had left home for his usual walk that day wearing a high-vis jacket.

‌



View 3 Images Dad-of-two Aaron Jones died at the scene (Image: media Wales)

Aaron's family at first thought he was missing. His wife Lisa had received a phone call from a member of the public who found their dog in the road with no owner, according to Wales Online.

Swansea Crown Court heard on March 30 that a "frantic search" ensued, with friends and family all searching for Aaron, 38, who had left home just a short time before the incident. The crash had made a loud noise, so a member of the public nearby at the time went to see what happened.

‌



He said he saw the takeaway driver's vehicle had stopped around 50 yards down the road. Wyke had started to pick up debris, including his bumper, from around his car. The driver then told the man that he had hit a branch or a tree but said he didn't know who the dog belonged to.

View 3 Images Wyke carried on delivering Chinese takeaways after he hit the dad (Image: Media Wales)

The Chinese takeaway driver then saw the dad's body over the stone wall but did not call the police or an ambulance. Wyke left the scene and carried on delivering food but arrived back at the crash site 10-20 minutes later and spoke to the same man, who told him the dog's owner was on her way. The driver left again and went to the restaurant where he worked and, while outside, shared to another delivery driver that his car crashed into a branch.

‌



Prosecutor Ian Wright said Wyke seemed visibly agitated at this point, adding: "He kicked his car and swore. He told the delivery driver that he only had third party insurance and so he didn't know how he would fund the repairs."

Meanwhile Aaron Jones' friends and family had launched a search in the area then one of his friends looked over the wall and saw Aaron's high-vis jacket. They started CPR and carried this on until the first responders arrived, however by this point it was too late, and Aaron was tragically pronounced dead.

Wyke had gone and swapped his damaged car for his dad's car before carrying on with his deliveries, finishing his shift at around 10.30pm. Acting in Wyke's defence, Mr Dyfed Thomas said that Wyke had "lied in a panic" and told the court that he is neurodivergent.

‌



After CCTV enquiries and forensic officers matched green fibres from his car's windshield to Aaron's high-vis jacket, Wykes was arrested the following afternoon at around 3pm, on December 24. Wykes was sentenced on March 30 to four and a half years in prison for the offence of causing death by dangerous driving.

After sentencing, His Honour Judge Paul Thomas KC said: "Had you been looking he would've been visible to you for about 100 metres or more. To put that into context, the length of a rugby pitch. You clearly were not looking down the road otherwise you would have seen him for a considerable distance. After you hit Mr Jones with your car at 34mph or thereabouts it must've been obvious to you that you had hit someone and caused them very serious injury.

"In the highly unlikely event that you were not aware at the moment of impact, which in itself means that you weren't looking along the road for considerable distance, the presence of the dog and your decision to look over the wall leads me to the conclusion that you quite simply decided to prioritise evading responsibility for what you have done, with the obviously serious injury that you would have caused the pedestrian, rather than than try to give him any help or even attempt to call for help.

Article continues below

"That in my view, Mr Wyke, was cruelly inhumane. It will not ever be known whether the intervention might have saved his life, but you didn't even take that chance, because you were far more intent on your own skin so you drove off leaving him dead or dying while you simply carried on with your deliveries with the bumper of your car hanging off and a shattered windscreen on the driver side.

"Those close to Mr Jones were frantically searching for him. The anguish they were feeling at the time was simply unimaginable. However at the same time, you were concerned about the financial cost for you in terms of repairing your car as you only had third-party insurance."

News.title: Russia hit by brutal crime wave after Putin frees criminals to fight in Ukraine war
News.content:
Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine is fuelling a surge in brutal crime inside Russia after criminals freed to fight.

A dramatic explosion in killings and sex crime accusations by military personnel is revealed in shocking new statistics which are on an unprecedented scale.

Analysis of Russia’s garrison military courts found that since the start of the full-scale invasion, servicemen have committed at least 729 murders — a staggering increase of 662 compared to the four years before the war, with civilians the most likely victims.

Image: Chita.ru/ East2west News) Chita.ru/ East2west News)

At the same time, sexual violence is soaring, with nine times more rapes, and a quintupling of other cases involving “violent sexual acts”.

Of an analysis of 549 cases in military courts involving Putin fighters - many released from serious sentences in jail to take part in the war - 312 involve sex crimes committed against minors, including 249 against those under the age of 14.

The stark statistics show how the Kremlin’s war is corroding life inside Russia, quite apart from the horror it has unleashed in Ukraine. In 2025, the military courts heard 352 murder cases, 35 times more than in 2018, before the war. Fatal violent assault is up ninefold, showed the statistics from independent Vot Tak channel.

Veteran Soviet and Russian commander, retired Colonel-General Leonid Ivashov, 82, warned that the brutality of the war is now poisoning Russian society. “This cruelty… this brutality is taking root and living among us,” he said. “The violence that is being demonstrated on the battlefield… is penetrating inside society as well…. We are already feeling it, and we will continue to feel it.”

Image: Social media/east2west news) Social media/east2west news)

He compared conditions for many soldiers to a “concentration camp”, describing men trapped in endless contracts and repeated deployments. With civilian courts also dealing with crimes involving Putin fighters, it is estimated the toll of shame of civilians killed by war returnees is now well over 1,000.

Putin has released tens of thousands of killers, rapists and thugs on condition that they are conscripted into the Russian armed forces. Many who commit these crimes then serve no punishment - because they are sent back to the frontline.

They can dodge jail at any stage – during the investigation, mid-trial or even after sentencing – by returning to fight.

Among the appalling crimes against civilians committed by Putin’s thuggish fighters include Tsyren-Dorzhi Tsyrenzhapov, who was recruited to war in Ukraine from jail where he was serving a 14-year sentence for murder, killed a woman, 22, in an argument, and later dismembered her body.

Putin soldier Andrey Gorlyakov, 41, raped and killed his niece Tatiana Naumova, 16, hiding her body in a forest, then took part in the search for the missing teenager. He was jailed for 20 years.

Alexei Nakvakin, a mobilised serviceman, killed a woman with a Kalashnikov rifle during an argument. She did not approve of the war in Ukraine.

Ex-convict Ivan Rossomakhin, 28, returned from the war to his home village in Kirov region and killed his neighbour Yulia Buiskykh, 85, at her home, it was alleged.

Volunteer fighter Alexander Mamayev, 44, stabbed his wife Ekaterina to death in front of their children on a break from fighting in Ukraine. Putin mercenary Demyan Kevorkyan, 31, and accomplices killed two, it is alleged.

Vasily Murachev, 33, a mercenary with an extensive criminal history, shot dead one person and wounded another in a cafe in Angarsk, Irkutsk region. Igor Sofonov, 38, a convict recruited to the Russian defence ministry’s Storm Z detachment killed six people with an accomplice, it was alleged.

Svetlana, 38, was brutally beaten by her boyfriend Sergei who fought in Ukraine from 2022. The woman slipped into a coma and passed away in hospital a week after the beating. Vladimir Vlasov, 31, a mercenary beat his stepdaughter Katia, four, to death, on his return from Ukraine.

News.title: Surprising reason Beatrice and Eugenie were banned from speaking to Harry and William
News.content:
Surprising reason Beatrice and Eugenie were banned from speaking to Harry and William

Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie were reportedly banned from seeing Prince William and Prince Harry after Princess Diana fell out with Sarah Ferguson over an astonishing claim

View 4 Images Beatrice and Eugenie were reportedly banned from speaking to Harry and William (Image: PA)

Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie were allegedly barred from contact with their cousins following a "falling out". This occurred after Princess Diana is said to have declared them "persona non grata" following a dispute with Sarah Ferguson.

‌



Royal biographer Tina Brown portrayed the York sisters as Prince William and Prince Harry's "favourite" cousins in her 2022 book, The Palace Papers. Fergie though is believed to have clashed with Diana after suggesting "she had developed verrucae after borrowing her shoes". According to The Times, it marked one of the earliest occasions the sisters recognised "families are not always happy".

‌



It states: "On top of their parents' divorce, they were banned from seeing their cousins William and Harry after Princess Diana fell out with Fergie over a verruca. (Fergie claimed she'd got one from borrowing Diana's shoes.)"

‌



According to WomanandHome, the episode formed part of Diana's "pattern of cutting out people" from the young princes' lives. Brown suggests this was something that "continued throughout their childhood".

The writer maintains that their mother "always needed to be first in her boys' hearts". She argues that while Diana was "clearly devoted" to the young princes, there existed a "destructive side to her mothering"

View 4 Images Beatrice and Eugenie are said to be Harry and William's 'favourite' cousins (Image: Getty)

‌



Beatrice and Eugenie have meanwhile experienced a turbulent journey within the Royal Family. Their parents separated in 1996, yet maintained a close bond, frequently being characterised as the "happiest divorced couple in the world". However, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah have faced ongoing scrutiny over their association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, who died in prison in 2019. Andrew's close ties with Epstein led to a catastrophic Newsnight interview in 2019.

Beatrice was reportedly "left in tears" after the interview, which she is said to have helped arrange. Former producer Sam McAlister claims Beatrice was an "unexpected guest" in the discussions ahead of the programme.

She disclosed that Beatrice posed "sensible questions" about the suggestions from Newsnight staff and later expressed sympathy for the princess as her father "discussed his relationship" with Epstein.

‌



View 4 Images Sarah reportedly fell out with Diana over a verruca (Image: Getty)

According to the Mail on Sunday, Beatrice hosted a birthday dinner for her then-fiancé, now husband Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi shortly after the interview aired. A source noted she was "quite tearful at times".

They added: "In fact, Beatrice has been in tears every day since the interview went out."

‌



Since then, Andrew has been stripped of his royal titles and military patronages and compelled to vacate his Royal Lodge residence. The former Duke of York shared the 30-room mansion with Sarah. Sarah and Andrew are reportedly known to consult their daughter when making public-facing decisions.

View 4 Images Beatrice and Eugenie won't be attending the Royal Family Easter service (Image: Getty)

A source told the Mail on Sunday: "Both Sarah and Andrew rely on Beatrice's judgement a lot when it comes to dealing with the public as she's got an old head on young shoulders. You can't really blame Beatrice because I think the odds were stacked against her on this one."

Article continues below

It comes as Beatrice, 37, and Eugenie, 36, are expected to be absent from the Royal Family Easter service this weekend. The York sisters have made separate arrangements away from Windsor, but have not been "frozen out" from the occasion.

News.title: 'I caught meningitis on Tenerife holiday - I would've died if I got on flight'
News.content:
'I caught meningitis on Tenerife holiday - I would've died if I got on flight'

Jade Bird, 33, has said she 'probably would've died' if she caught her scheduled flight on the day she began developing meningitis symptoms on holiday in Tenerife

View 3 Images Jade Bird, 33, contracted meningitis while on holiday in Tenerife (Image: Joanne McIver / SWNS)

A mum who caught meningitis on holiday in Tenerife has admitted she 'probably would have died' if she hadn't abandoned her plans to fly.

‌



Jade Bird, 33, was due to fly home from the Spanish holiday island last Wednesday - but fell seriously ill at the airport after contracting the illness on holiday. She was then rushed from the airport to hospital, where doctors found an infection in her brain that had developed into meningitis.

‌



Jade, a carer who now lives in Abergele, Wales, spent eight days in an induced coma and another 10 days on intravenous antibiotics. But she's now on the mend after returning to Britain, and has been reunited with her six-year-old daughter Skyla.

‌



View 3 Images Mum Jade has now been reunited with her six-year-old daughter Skyla (Image: Joanne McIver / SWNS)

Major update on Brit who was fighting for life in Tenerife with meningitis READ MORE :

Speaking for the first time after returning home, she told the Manchester Evening News: "I still have to have more procedures, I have to have a lumbar puncture. But I'm in a much better state than I was, considering what I've been through."

Jade says she doesn't remember much of her ordeal, adding: "I must have been in that much pain that I had no memory, but I have had problems with my ears since 2021, and I struggle with altitudes. On Tenerife I travelled around the island, I went up Masca valley and to Mount Teide, and my ears were absolutely killing. I think that altitude is where it all began.

‌



"I remember coming down from the mountain and starting to be sick. That day I was getting ready to get on the airport transfer. I remember asking my boyfriend to pass me a bag so I could be sick, and that's the last thing I remember. My boyfriend remembers me locking myself in the toilet - apparently I was screaming in the airport. I'm glad I never got on the flight. If I did, I probably would have died."

View 3 Images Doctors have told her it could take her months to recover after she emerged from an eight-day coma (Image: Joanne McIver / SWNS)

Jade spent a total of 18 days in hospital before being discharged on March 26 and flying home the same day. In the meantime, her friends and family set up a GoFundMe page, which covered the costs of Jade's loved ones flying out to visit her, raising over £13,000.

‌



"When I woke up and looked on my phone, I couldn't believe everything that I was seeing," she said. "Everyone's support was so overwhelming but so beautiful. I am still overwhelmed by it now. I can't believe how much support I had. I cry about it and I've lost all my street cred. Everyone was saying, jade will get through this, she's a fighter. All those comments were so beautiful and it's kept me going."

Jade has been told by doctors it may take her months to recover. "My hearing is pretty poor and my hands are really weak", she explained. "I've got memory loss and some swelling on my brain still. It's going to be a long process."

Her medical bills reached the tens of thousands, but this was thankfully paid for by her insurance. "I was in a coma, we didn't know how long I would be unconscious for," she said. "The GoFundMe has enabled my family to get endless flights and stay at my bedside. They didn't know if I was going to die or not. It's also let me stay off work to recover properly and spend time with my daughter until I'm better."

Article continues below

Jade also plans on making a donation to Tommy's Journey, a fundraiser for a five-year-old boy from Sale suffering from an aggressive form of cancer.

"I'm poorly but I know he needs it more than me," she said. "I feel like helping him is helping others in the same way that they helped me. Normally I'd never be able to donate so much."

Boxing.title: 'A nose bleed in the ring saved my life': Rising star REUBEN MUSTON reveals his extraordinary journey since a rare illness nearly killed him - and how he became the first pro boxer to fight after having a stem cell transplant
Boxing.content:
'A nose bleed in the ring saved my life': Rising star REUBEN MUSTON reveals his extraordinary journey since a rare illness nearly killed him - and how he became the first pro boxer to fight after having a stem cell transplant

Fighting for money doesn’t hold nearly the same fear as fighting for your life. Reuben Muston is better placed than most to make the distinction.

‘I’m just happy to be here,’ he says, and it’s a summary that serves only a modicum of justice to a remarkable tale.

You see, Muston became a professional boxer this month, which is common enough. But where his situation differs is the background - no British fighter before him has crossed to the paid ranks after undergoing a stem cell transplant.

He will explain the gravity and science behind that situation in his own words. And why he would most likely be dead if it wasn’t for a nosebleed that ran for the better part of five days.

But to get there, Muston first goes back to February 12, 2022 and a leisure centre in Barnsley. It was the semi-final of the England Youth Championships and Muston, a lad of 17 from Reading and one of the country’s best amateur flyweights, was up against Mikie Tallon. Big fight, big opportunity.

‘I was quite clearly up on the scorecards but towards the end of the second round, we clash heads,’ says Muston. ‘I go back to the corner and there is blood everywhere from my nose.

'I'm just happy to be here,' says boxer Reuben Muston (pictured with his dad Danny), three years on from the pair's stem cell transplant that saved his life

Former world champion Anthony Crolla is one of the informed cohort of observers who believe Muston could make waves in the sport

‘The third round, it’s still bleeding. OK. Well, the ref stops us a couple of times, gets the doctor to take a look and then, with about 30 seconds left, he tells me, “I can't let you go on any more”. Honestly, the ring, me and Mikie were covered in blood.

‘It shattered my heart. That championship was meant to be my break and I’m devastated. So I go home that night and for some reason my nose is still bleeding. Bleeding on me, my dinner, everything. It hadn’t stopped by the time I went to bed.’

As it transpires, packing his nose with tissue wasn’t the solution. Muston recalls: ‘When I got up it was like a murder scene – blood all over my sheets, all up the walls.

‘My dad took one look at me and said we’re going to A&E. They did hours of tests and after a while a doctor took us to a private room. They suspected it might be leukaemia, but under the microscope it didn’t look how it should.’

That meant more tests. Many of them. Across the span of three days, specialists of all denominations came and went. While this was happening, the bleeding did not stop.

Eventually, one of the tests, a biopsy on his bone marrow, zeroed in on a reason - aplastic anaemia. Exceptionally rare, it’s a life-threatening blood disorder that causes the marrow to stop producing enough new blood cells and affects between two and six people per million. Muston was exceptionally unlucky, save for one fact – the good fortune of a nosebleed that led to the diagnosis.

Muston: ‘The most basic way of explaining it is what I was told. So your platelet count should be between 150,000 and 400,000 (per microlitre) and your haemoglobin should be between 120 and 150 (per litre of blood) but I had a platelet count of 1,000 and my haemoglobin was 55. Below 50 and you can go into cardiac arrest.

‘The doctors said, “In two weeks, you could have had a massive brain haemorrhage or cardiac arrest and you would have been dead”, essentially. Really, the nosebleed saved my life.’

After days of tests, Muston was eventually diagnosed with aplastic anaemia - a rare blood disorder that affects just two to six people in every million

‘The doctors said, “In two weeks, you could have had a massive brain haemorrhage or cardiac arrest and you would have been dead”'
